content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I want to connect [product_name] as a third-party device using RS or Ethernet, but I'm unsure if this is possible. If not, should I change the [product_name], or is there a communication module available? My [product_name] is ([article_no]) and it is linked to an operator display. Any advice would be appreciated.

Can you clarify what devices you want to connect? The [product_name] [article_no] does not support RS or Ethernet. However, you can use expansion modules like EIB/KNX or AS-I. The newer [product_name] versions ([article_no]) are Ethernet-capable and can communicate with controllers that support the S7-200 protocol.
I want to connect an ABB AC500 PLC to display data from [product_name] on a SCADA system related to the AC500. I'm not sure how to do this—could you guide me through the process? Thanks in advance.
From what I know, it's not possible for a [product_name] with [article_no] to communicate with ABB 500 PLC, since [product_name] [article_no] lacks bus or Ethernet connectivity.
Thank you for your help. As you mentioned, the only communication option is through an S7 (CPU), correct? Are there any other ways to retrieve this data? Thanks.

Yes, the [product_name] [article_no] versions can communicate with S7-300 and S7-1200 CPUs as they support the S7-200 protocol. The [product_name] [article_no] cannot do this. You can find examples at: [url]

So expansion modules like EIB/KNX or AS-I only allow communication with S7 CPUs, correct? If I want to solve this, I should have an S7 CPU collect data from [product_name] devices and then connect the S7 to the ABB AC500 CPU, right? Which CPUs are compatible? Thanks.
Sorry, I'm unable to assist further. I can't specify which S7 models communicate with both [product_name] and ABB AC500. I'm unfamiliar with ABB500 and its supported protocols (Profibus or others).

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are trying to enable data exchange between an older [product_name] module and an ABB AC500 PLC for use in a SCADA system. The lack of RS or Ethernet ports on the [product_name] ([article_no]) means direct integration is not possible. Later [product_name] versions include Ethernet support, enabling broader device compatibility. The communication limitations of the older model have led to user uncertainty and frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: The user aims to connect the older [product_name] ([article_no]) with a third-party PLC and achieve SCADA integration, ideally via standard communication methods like RS or Ethernet, or through an appropriate expansion module.
